title: Question 3
stem:
A uniform beam AB is attached by a hinge to a wall at end A, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1}}

The beam has length $0.50\text{ m}$ and weight $W$. A block of weight $12\text{ N}$ rests on the beam at a distance of $0.15\text{ m}$ from end B.

The beam is held horizontal and in equilibrium by a string attached between end B and a fixed point C. The string has a tension of $17\text{ N}$ and is at an angle of $50^{\circ}$ to the horizontal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State **two** conditions for an object to be in equilibrium.

markscheme_points.text: resultant force (in any direction) is zero
resultant moment/torque (about any point) is zero

hints: Hint 1: Think about what equilibrium means for motion - first for moving from place to place, then for spinning or turning.
Hint 2: Recall the two separate vector sums that must both vanish, one for forces and one for turning effects about any point.
parts.proper_answer: 1. The resultant force on the object is zero. 2. The resultant moment about any point is zero.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **No translation means balanced forces**
Imagine sitting beside the beam. If it is not accelerating left, right, up or down, all the pushes and pulls must cancel out. That means the vector sum of all forces is zero.

Step 2: **No rotation means balanced moments**
Even with zero net force, an object could still spin. For no angular acceleration, clockwise moments must exactly balance anticlockwise moments. So $$\text{resultant moment about any point} = 0$$

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Show that the vertical component of the tension in the string is $13\text{ N}$.
hints: Hint 1: Picture the 17 N tension arrow at 50 degrees above the horizontal and focus on which side of the right-angled triangle gives the vertical part.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Resolve the tension**
The string pulls at $50^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. The vertical side is opposite the angle, so it uses sine: $$T_v = T \sin 50^{\circ}$$ $$T_v = 17 \times \sin 50^{\circ} = 13.0\text{ N} \approx 13\text{ N}$$

enrichment.label: (b)
hints: Hint 1: Picture the 17 N tension arrow at 50 degrees above the horizontal and focus on which side of the right-angled triangle gives the vertical part.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Resolve the tension**
The string pulls at $50^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. The vertical side is opposite the angle, so it uses sine: $$T_v = T \sin 50^{\circ}$$ $$T_v = 17 \times \sin 50^{\circ} = 13.0\text{ N} \approx 13\text{ N}$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: By taking moments about end A, calculate the weight $W$ of the beam.
hints: Hint 1: Taking moments about A removes the hinge forces - think where the weight of a uniform beam acts and what the distances are for $W$, the 12 N block and the 13 N lift at B.
Hint 2: Set the total clockwise moment equal to the total anticlockwise moment about A and rearrange to isolate $W$ before using numbers.
parts.proper_answer: Taking moments about A: $W \times 0.25 + 12 \times 0.35 = 13 \times 0.50$, giving $W = 9.2\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Choose pivot A to simplify**
Moments about A mean the unknown hinge forces have zero moment. For a uniform 0.50 m beam, weight $W$ acts at the centre, 0.25 m from A. The 12 N block is 0.35 m from A. The upward 13 N force at B is 0.50 m from A.

Step 2: **Balance clockwise and anticlockwise moments**
Clockwise moments are due to weights pulling down: $$(W \times 0.25) + (12 \times 0.35)$$ Anticlockwise moment is due to the string pulling up: $$(13 \times 0.50)$$ In equilibrium: $$(W \times 0.25) + (12 \times 0.35) = 13 \times 0.50$$ $$W \times 0.25 = 6.5 - 4.2 = 2.3$$ $$W = \frac{2.3}{0.25} = 9.2\text{ N}$$

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the vertical component of the force exerted on the beam by the hinge.
hints: Hint 1: In the vertical direction the beam does not move, so compare the total upward forces with the total downward forces on the beam.
parts.proper_answer: Vertical hinge force $F = W + 12 - 13 = 9.2 + 12 - 13 = 8.2\text{ N}$ upward, magnitude about $8\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Balance up and down**
Upward forces are the 13 N component from the string plus the vertical hinge force $F$. Downward forces are $W$ and 12 N. With zero resultant force: $$F + 13 = W + 12$$ $$F = 9.2 + 12 - 13 = 8.2\text{ N}$$ This is about $8\text{ N}$ upward on the beam.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The block is now moved closer to end A of the beam. Assume that the beam remains horizontal.

State whether this change will increase, decrease or have no effect on the horizontal component of the force exerted on the beam by the hinge.
hints: Hint 1: Think about which force must balance the sideways pull of the string at the hinge, and how moving the block changes the moment balance and hence the tension needed.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link horizontal hinge force to tension**
Horizontally, the only forces are the horizontal component of string tension pulling one way and the hinge pushing the other, so they must be equal in size. Moving the block toward A reduces its clockwise moment, so a smaller anticlockwise moment and smaller tension is needed to keep balance. A smaller tension means a smaller horizontal component, so the horizontal hinge force decreases.
